items_missed: Save Your Ass prep speech completely absent — and the customer handed him the opening twice. 'We can take the bar stools on our own. We're just more so looking for like taking the big stuff' was an invitation to run the whole prep speech, and the reply was 'We'll focus on the bulky items for you, for sure.' That is agreeing with the customer instead of coaching him.

On-Time Guarantee never mentioned on a 1:30 afternoon booking. He explained the arrival window and the guarantee in detail on his other call the same day, so this is inconsistency, not a knowledge gap.

Meet Your Mover never pitched. He talked about a specific mover (Miles) at length and tried to request him, which is great rapport but does not cover the pre-move email with the mover's photo and info.

Box count never resolved. He opened with 'you have eighty boxes. Does that sound accurate?', the customer said 'I'm not sure, I don't think it's gonna be that many,' and the number was never pinned down — on an hourly job where box count is a primary time driver.
Packing services never offered or priced. A customer with an unknown box count and three bedrooms is the exact profile for a packing pitch.
No 'pricing is super simple' opener — he went straight from inventory into $111 per mover per hour with no framing.

15-minute prorated increments never explained. He quoted a flat $1,185 against a padded 5-hour estimate and never told the customer they only pay for time actually used — so the padding reads as a price instead of a ceiling.
What's-included list was partial: covered pads, blankets, shrink wrap and no supply cost, but never named gas, truck, taxes, insurance, bands or tools.
No 'no hidden fees' pitch (no credit card fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees) — only the deposit and cancellation-fee pieces.
Never asked about garage, attic, patio, or storage-unit contents. He went room by room through three bedrooms, living room and kitchen and stopped there, on a whole-house move.
Never asked about stairs at the origin home in Kyle — the destination stairs were probed thoroughly, the pickup side wasn't asked about at all.
Never asked 'is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?'
No volume equivalent used (school bus reference or similar) to help a customer with a fuzzy box count picture the job.
Ecobox referral not made despite an unresolved box count and an obvious need for boxes.
Customer's name never used once in 16.8 minutes — the greeting was a garbled 'Mister us' and the close was 'man'.
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' — he offered a callback instead, and gave no hours of operation.

Promised to request Miles, then had to walk it back twice ('Sorry, I kinda spoke too soon' / 'it doesn't look like miles is working that day') — plus an audible fumble on the estimate ('Sorry I said five hours like it was trying to change my estimate').
top_strength: The estimate build was genuinely excellent and is the reason this call scored above his other one. He pulled the customer's prior move, saw it had actually run three and three quarter hours, and then reasoned out loud about why he would not simply reuse that number: 'granted miles is a very talented individual... I would be remiss if I tried to schedule it for about that same time.' He set the estimate at five and a half hours against a four-and-a-half-hour expectation and named the padding explicitly — 'about an hour wiggle room... to help compensate for the drive time in between locations.' He also volunteered the rate increase before the customer could notice it ('Instead of $100 it's going to be $111'), proactively surfaced a courtyard access problem from personal knowledge of the building ('I actually used to live at that complex'), and broke out the $75 trip fee and confirmed it was already inside the $1,185 rather than a surprise on top. The room-by-room inventory — TV mounted or not, sectional or one piece, adjustable bed base, power cords with the monitors — was the most disciplined probing on either of his calls.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: the customer said 'we're just more so looking for like taking the big stuff' and Hector agreed with him instead of running the prep speech. That sentence is a live buying signal for Save Your Ass and it is a ten-point section he took a zero on. The language: 'Ivan, that instinct is exactly right, and let me push it further — every carload you take yourself comes straight off the clock. Kids' toys, loose stuff in drawers, photos off the walls, anything small consolidated into totes in one room. On a five-hour estimate that prep can genuinely be thirty to forty-five minutes off your bill. Does that make sense?' Second priority: he never resolved the box count. He asked, got 'I'm not sure, I don't think it's gonna be that many,' and moved on — on an hourly job. Push once: 'No problem, roughly — are we talking ten, thirty, fifty? And do you want us to handle the packing, or are you boxing it yourself?' That one follow-up unlocks the box count, the packing pitch, and the Ecobox referral, three things he lost points on from the same missed question. Third: he explained the arrival window and On-Time Guarantee beautifully on his San Antonio call two hours earlier and skipped both here on a 1:30 afternoon slot. That is a consistency problem — the guarantee should be automatic on every afternoon booking. Last thing, and it is free points: he padded the estimate by an hour for safety, which is smart, but he never told the customer they only pay for the time actually used in fifteen-minute increments. Say it right after the total, or the padding lands as a price instead of protection.
phone_presence_notes: Real rapport rather than scripted warmth — he connected over having lived in the customer's complex, dug up the prior move, and tried to get the same mover back, and the customer reciprocated unprompted with 'this is a great, great service I just wanted to give you guys a callback' and 'Likewise bye-bye'; held back from a 5 by zero name use and heavy verbal tics ('to that end', 'rest assured is like') plus a couple of visible fumbles.
